acceptance.expected: CI rejects a commit with a file matching secret patterns (`*.pem`, `.env`, the PEM private key header string from the plan)
acceptance.actual: check_secrets.py reports ANY occurrence of a PEM private key header (five dashes, BEGIN, optional words, PRIVATE KEY; case-insensitive, no trailing dashes needed) anywhere in any file, including UTF-16 and binary. File-name patterns are matched case-insensitively. Exceptions: only the exact path docs/implementation-plan-v1.md (quotes the AC; the plan must not be edited) plus two pinned historical (path, Git blob SHA) pairs for cycle-1 reports already in the pushed branch history (needed so the PR range scan is not permanently red without rewriting history); any other content at those paths is scanned. tests/ci/test_check_secrets.py: 43 tests incl. the critic's cases (one-line key after KEY=, PRIVATE_KEY=<header>, k = '<header>' in .py, KEY.PEM, server.Pem, .ENV, Server.Key) and an allowlist test proving the same text at any other path is caught. Branch scan origin/main..HEAD and tree HEAD: clean.
evidence: CI job `secrets`: tree of HEAD + every commit of the PR/push; on force-push (unreachable push.before) scans origin/main..HEAD with a notice
